findings.title: Unexpected exceptions skip the cutover report the docstring promises
findings.description:
The module docstring says the first failure stops the run and "the report is still written". `run_steps` only catches `StepFailed` and `CalledProcessError`. Several steps can raise other exceptions, and those escape `main()` before `report.write_text(...)` runs:
- `run_health` (lines 157-165) guards with `log.exists()`, but an existing empty log makes `splitlines()[-1]` raise `IndexError`.
- `step_production` (line 224) reads the production health log with no existence or emptiness check. That is `FileNotFoundError` or `IndexError`.
- `conf_sums` in `cutover_227_host.py` uses `next(...)` with no default, so it raises `StopIteration`.
- `tick_locks_held` calls `int(psql(...))`, which raises `ValueError` on unexpected output.

A cutover that dies mid-way on a production host then leaves no `<date>-227-cutover.md`, which is the one record of what was seen. Convert these into `require(...)` failures, or catch `(OSError, IndexError, ValueError, StopIteration)` in `run_steps` with the same record-and-stop treatment.

`run_health` (line 164) and `block_commands` also use `assert x is not None` for type narrowing in production code. `python -O` strips those asserts. Making `require` return `NoReturn` on failure, or raising explicitly, would remove the need.

findings.title: Gaps in the cutover tests, and one weakened assertion
findings.description:
The tests cover the pure helpers, `step_weekly`, `step_restart`, `step_switch` and `step_production` well. The steps that gate production safety have no test:
- `step_apply`, which runs the "production cron lines gain only the new args" gate through `production_changes`.
- `step_check`, `step_guards` and `step_offsite`, including the `--min-age` arithmetic for `wal/`.
- `run_health` with a missing or empty log. This is the failure in the previous finding.
- `main()`'s cron-user and bucket guards.

Two smaller test-quality points:
- `test/unit/test_setup_backup.py` has `assert "@" not in text.replace("@192", "")`. I found no `@192` anywhere under `deploy/`, so the replace appears to be a leftover. It weakens the unfilled-placeholder assertion it sits in. Restore `"@" not in text`.
- `test/unit/test_provision_tick_lib.py` asserts source text. Examples are `'-v with_replication=1 -f - < "$ROLES_SQL"' in body` and the `CREATED_DATABASES=(trading_tick)` literal. These check how the script is written, not what it does. They break on harmless reformatting and don't catch a behavioral regression. The `hba_content` render test is the better pattern.

findings.title: Host constants and a log-format contract are repeated across languages
findings.description:
CLAUDE.md says a value used in comparisons or lookups should be defined once. Several are now spelled in more than one place:
- `HOST_BACKUP_ROOT = Path("/data/backup")` in `cutover_227_host.py`. It also appears as 17/main's `backup_root` in `deploy/backup-clusters.conf`, and as the `--backup-root` the cutover hands to `setup-backup.sh`.
- `RCLONE_REMOTE = "b2"` in the cutover and `RCLONE_REMOTE=b2` in `setup-backup.sh`.
- `ARM_FILE = "RECONCILE-ARMED"` in the cutover, `setup-backup.sh`, and the `--armed` path in `manta-trading-backup.cluster`.
- `MT_BACKUP_S3_BUCKET` in `b2_lifecycle.sh` (`BUCKET_KEY`), `setup-backup.sh` and `cutover_227_host.py`.
- `step_weekly` (line 176) skips on `base/<datetime.now():%Y%m%d>`. That silently depends on `cron_weekly_backup.sh:123` using `date +%Y%m%d`. If the format drifts, the skip never fires. A same-day or later re-run then executes the weekly job again, and once the arm file exists that includes the armed reconcile.

The two config parsers (`backup_clusters.sh` and `backup_clusters.py`) also duplicate rule logic. The parity test mitigates this and the cross-language split is understandable. Still, add a comment at each duplicated constant naming its twin, or have the cutover read the shared values from one place.

findings.title: `ensure_dir` defines helpers that leak and rely on dynamic scope
findings.description: `ensure_dir` defines `dir_ok`, `dir_make`, `shape_ok` and `shape_fix` inside the function, and they read its `local` variables through bash dynamic scoping. After it returns they remain global functions pointing at unset variables, which would hit `set -u` if anything called them. This works today. `host_dir_ok` was renamed to avoid a clash, which shows the namespace is already shared. Passing `dir`, `owner` and `mode` as arguments, or `unset -f` at the end, would harden it.

findings.title: Replication grant and pg_hba entry are scoped and opt-in
findings.description: `REPLICATION` is granted to `tick_migrate` only when `-v with_replication=1` is passed, and `provision_tick_cluster.sh` passes it. pg_hba admits `replication` for that one role from the client source address, over scram-sha-256. This mirrors `provision_roles.sql` and is well documented in the file. The role is also the general maintenance role, so it can stream the whole cluster; that is inherent to using `pg_basebackup` over the maintenance URL.

findings.title: Placeholder rendering, cluster-table validation and lifecycle checking are sound
findings.description:
I checked the following against the actual files:
- `##` template comments are stripped before rendering.
- `@CLUSTER@` cannot prefix-collide with `@CLUSTER_ROOT@`.
- Replacements are quoted, so the bash 5.2 `&` behaviour can't corrupt `2>&1`.
- Host-level substitutions run after the cluster blocks are inserted, so block placeholders are still filled.
- The unfilled-placeholder and unescaped-`%` guards run on the final text.
- The cluster table is parsed before any step in `setup-backup.sh`.
- `pg_lsclusters` supplies the data directory.
- `b2_lifecycle.sh` is read-only (the rclone call has no `-o` option), validates `--days`, and passes credentials only in the child's environment.
- `setup-backup.sh` does not count a missing lifecycle rule as a failure, but does count an unreadable rule set.
- The arming flow in `step_weekly` matches TD7 in the slice design.

structured_findings.summary: Unexpected exceptions skip the cutover report the docstring promises
Gaps in the cutover tests, and one weakened assertion
Host constants and a log-format contract are repeated across languages
`ensure_dir` defines helpers that leak and rely on dynamic scope
Replication grant and pg_hba entry are scoped and opt-in
Placeholder rendering, cluster-table validation and lifecycle checking are sound
